speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether bus shelter address plates can display the bus stop code, instead of the LTA alpha-numeric code, to assist bus passengers in identifying bus stops in advance of arriving at a particular bus stop; and (b) what measures has LTA taken to make navigation easier for bus passengers, including people with disabilities and the less technology-savvy.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: And I thank the Senior Minister of State for the answer.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I understand that the bus stop codes and names are displayed at the bus stop pole and the bus stop information board.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: However, the font that is used is relatively small and it is not easily visible to passengers as they are approaching the bus stop.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, it would not give them enough time to be able to press the button to indicate to the bus captain to stop the bus.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: In fact, the most prominent signage at the bus stop is actually the bus shelter address plate, which is on the top of the bus shelter because the font can be seen from quite a distance away, about 40 metres away at least, in my estimation.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, this will give the commuters a bit more time to prepare to stop, to press the bell to stop the bus.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: One analogy that I could give is this: it is a little bit like our postal code.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we refer to a particular block, let us say in my area Block 130A Lorong 1 Toa Payoh.
